why_this_tests_collapse: The existing axis-B fixtures each carry one rule class, so a reading pass that collapses onto whichever dimension it noticed first still scores recall 1.0 — the case cannot distinguish "found all three dimensions" from "found the only dimension present". This fixture carries all three classes at once, two defects each, and arranges them so that neither locality nor rule identity can be inferred from the other. No section holds two defects of the same rule: each of the three named sections (data model, components, interfaces) mixes two different rule classes, and each rule's pair is split across two different top-level sections. A reader who collapses onto rule 3 finds 2 of 6 and leaves both maxims and both coined nouns; one who collapses onto rule 6 (the most visually salient class, since a strange noun stands out) finds 2 of 6 and leaves both split obligations, which are the least salient because every sentence in them is short, plain and individually conforming. Recall therefore reads out as a per-rule vector rather than a single number: 2/2 on one class with 0/2 or 1/2 on the others is the Shaib et al. collapse signature, while 6/6 is the evidence that one combined B4 pass carries three dimensions and does not need splitting into three passes. The distribution also separates two failure shapes the single-rule fixtures cannot: a pass that reads only the sections already carrying an obvious defect (locality collapse) versus a pass that reads every section for only one rule (dimension collapse). Every planted defect sits in the declared recall gap of SKILL.md section 5 — connective split across sentences for rule 3, novel aphorisms matching no template for rule 4, nouns coined today for rule 6 — and the scanner reports 0 warn / 0 info over the whole 182-line document, so nothing in the mechanical pass points the reader at any of the six.
